skillShortcuts.title: Medical Research Skill Shortcuts
skillShortcuts.promptSingle:
Please use the {{skill}} skill to help me with this task.

Describe your task here:
skillShortcuts.promptMulti:
Please use the following skills for this task: {{skills}}.

Describe your research task here:

prompts.pipeline:
Please help me with "Study pathway planning". First decide whether the current content is a literature question, registry cohort, paper reproduction, existing data analysis, or manuscript output; then break the work into evidence, data, pre-analysis, statistical modeling, results integration, and submission/presentation steps. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.deepResearch:
Please help me with "Medical evidence search". First clarify PICO, disease/exposure/outcome, population boundary, time window, and evidence type; then organize search, screening, evidence matrix, research gaps, and database-study opportunities. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.deepLiteratureSearch:
Please help me with "Deep search". First decompose the question into keywords, synonyms, PICO elements, and evidence types; then choose the smallest necessary search tools, search strings, candidate papers, and a screening plan. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.literatureDatabases:
Please help me with "Literature databases". First decide whether PubMed, OpenAlex, or bioRxiv best fits the question; then provide search strings, screening rules, metadata fields, and an auditable result table. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.citationTrace:
Please help me with "Citation tracing". First verify core papers, DOIs, references, and citation chains; then identify key evidence, missing citations, citation errors, and target-venue citation output. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.paperReading:
Please help me with "Paper reading tools". First identify the papers to read or compare; then extract the question, design, inclusion/exclusion criteria, variable definitions, statistical models, figures, and reproducibility risks. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.researchMonitoring:
Please help me with "Research monitoring". First define topic, time window, sources, and exclusion rules; then summarize recent representative papers, trends, translatable questions, and the next monitoring recommendation. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.databaseAccess:
Please help me with "Database extraction". Use the 1 API base + 27 independent database skills + optional cross-database router pattern. Prefer api.medtimehelp.com and fall back to a healthy 127.0.0.1:8787 service only when the public endpoint is unavailable. Decide whether routing is needed; distinguish Chinese databases, SHARE/HRS-family, UKB, NHANES, ICU/EHR, perioperative, and cancer-registry sources; state structural risks such as patient/stay/wave/cycle/timeline/coding-era semantics, locate real tables and fields, and extract only task-needed variables with source paths. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.ideation:
Please help me with "Clinical study ideation". First evaluate evidence gap, available database, clinical relevance, and statistical feasibility; then form PICO, core hypothesis, novelty claim, candidate data source, main model, and minimum viable analysis. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.preAnalysis:
Please help me with "Data analysis". Inspect the data structure, variable types, missingness, outliers, and analysis objective first. Keep database-specific analyses, baseline tables, descriptive statistics, tests, and modeling in this category, select the smallest necessary skill set, and produce diagnostics, visualization, effect sizes, and reproducible outputs. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My data or analysis question:
prompts.statisticalModeling:
Please help me with "Statistical modeling and testing". Use only the selected skills and clarify the model/test target, variable roles, assumptions, diagnostics, effect sizes, and manuscript reporting for the current research question. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.medicalViz:
Please help me with "Medical visualization". Use only the skills I selected. First identify the figure type, then provide layout, palette, typography, legend, panel labels, figure-caption points, and PDF/PNG export requirements. Default journal-level figure design to nature-figure; pair clinical/biomedical statistical plots with data-visualization-biomedical; use scientific-visualization for general journal figure layout; use matplotlib, seaborn, plotly, or data-viz-plots only when lower-level plotting code is needed. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.resultsIntegration:
Please help me with "Results integration and drafting". First integrate existing Table 1, model outputs, figures, and sensitivity analyses; then organize main results, subgroups, robustness checks, interpretation boundaries, and submission-ready wording under STROBE/CONSORT logic. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.graphicalAbstract:
Please help me with "Graphical abstract". First distill the research question, data source, core method, key finding, and clinical implication; then propose a single-figure structure, visual hierarchy, icons/process elements, and submission-ready text. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.paperWriting:
Please help me with "Medical manuscript writing". First confirm target journal/article type, study design, primary results, and citation materials; use nature-data when drafting or auditing Data Availability statements, repository plans, dataset citations, or FAIR metadata; then proceed through Title, Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and reference validation. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.paperPolishing:
Please help me with "Manuscript polishing". First confirm target journal/article type, the sections or paragraphs to polish, and the tone (strict submission-ready vs slightly more human/natural). Default to nature-polishing for Nature-leaning academic English and section logic; use medhelp-humanizer when you need more natural, less templated phrasing and readability; pair with scientific-writing for IMRAD-level scientific prose; use citation-management to tighten references and citation formatting; use venue-templates to align structure and conventions with a specific journal or conference. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.paperReview:
Please help me with "Medical paper review". First check study design, statistical validity, evidence chain, causal language, figure/table consistency, and submission standards; then separate must-fix issues from recommended edits and acceptable content. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.grantWriting:
Please help me with "Medical grant writing". First clarify the scientific question, clinical/public-health significance, preliminary basis, innovation, aims, and technical route; then organize rationale, research plan, feasibility, and risk alternatives. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:
prompts.promotion:
Please help me with "Academic presentation and translation". First define audience, duration, core message, and available assets; then compress the paper into background, methods, results, clinical meaning, limitations, and next steps. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My task:

routePrompts.statisticalModeling:
Please help me with "Statistical modeling and testing". Route my statistical task to the smallest necessary skill set first. Do not call the entire skill group by default.

Routing rules:
1. Statistical analysis plan, test selection, hypotheses, effect sizes, power, APA or manuscript reporting: use statistical-analysis.
2. Directly running specified t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlations, non-parametric tests, or multiple-testing correction: use data-stats-analysis.
3. Linear, logistic, Poisson/negative binomial, mixed models, ARIMA/time series, robust standard errors, diagnostics, and coefficient tables: use statsmodels.
4. Cox, KM, survival outcomes, censored data, competing risks, or time-dependent AUC: use scikit-survival.
5. Bayesian, hierarchical, MCMC, prior/posterior predictive checks, or uncertainty quantification: use pymc.
6. UK Biobank-specific cohort fields, endpoints, covariates, and sensitivity analysis: use ukb-cohort-analysis.
7. Integrating finished statistical outputs, tables, figures, and Results text: use medhelp-experiment-analysis.

Default principles: for unclear clinical/epidemiologic analysis, start with statistical-analysis; add statsmodels, scikit-survival, or pymc only once the modeling target is clear.

First state the selected skill set and reason in one sentence, then start the work.

My task:
routePrompts.medicalVisualization:
Please help me with "Medical visualization". Route my medical visualization task to the smallest necessary skill set first. Do not call the entire visualization skill group by default.

Routing rules:
1. Journal-level layout, Nature/Lancet/JAMA style, multi-panel structure, palettes, and export requirements: use nature-figure.
2. Clinical/biomedical statistical figures, KM curves, forest plots, volcano plots, heatmaps, subgroup figures, or model-result displays: use data-visualization-biomedical.
3. General scientific figures, visual hierarchy, narrative figure design, and submission-ready visual conventions: use scientific-visualization.
4. Explicit Python plotting code or lower-level graphics control: use matplotlib, seaborn, plotly, or data-viz-plots as needed.

First identify the figure type, state the selected skill set and reason in one sentence, then provide layout, palette, typography, legend, panel labels, figure-caption points, and PDF/PNG export requirements.

My task:

prompts.researchIdeation:
Use the relevant research-ideation skills to develop a valuable, feasible topic. Evaluate clinical significance, evidence gaps, data availability, novelty, and statistical feasibility; then provide a PICO, core hypothesis, candidate data sources, and a minimum viable analysis. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My research direction:
prompts.readPaper:
Use paper-reading skills to help me analyze this paper. Extract the research question, design, eligibility criteria, variable definitions, statistical methods, key results, figures, limitations, and reproducibility risks, and distinguish the authors' claims from what the evidence actually supports. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Paper or file:
prompts.paperCard:
Use paper-card skills to produce a source-grounded deep analysis of one paper. Organize the research question, background route, pain point, core insight, method modules, essential formulas, experiment-to-claim evidence, conclusion boundaries, limitations, critical analysis, knowledge connections, and testable ideas as a structured Paper Card. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Paper, DOI, or file:
prompts.verifyReferences:
Use reference-verification skills to audit my citations one by one. Cross-check authors, title, year, volume, issue, pages, DOI, and source across multiple databases; separate must-fix, review-needed, and verified entries while preserving traceable sources. Never invent a citation. Available skills: {{skills}}.

References or manuscript to verify:
prompts.deepResearch:
Use deep-research skills to conduct a systematic, traceable investigation. Define the scope and evidence standard, search multiple sources, verify evidence, compare perspectives, identify gaps, and produce a structured report with sources. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My research topic:
prompts.writingAssistant:
Use the reduce-AI-rate skills to rewrite the text. First confirm the document type, target audience or journal, passages to edit, and tone. Use nature-polishing for Nature-leaning academic English and section logic; use medhelp-humanizer to remove templated phrasing and make the prose more natural; use citation-management to check citations, bibliography, and citation format, with nature-citation when a citation chain needs tracing. scientific-writing and nature-writing can still help with outlines, sections, or full drafts. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Text to de-AI:
prompts.makePresentation:
Use the most relevant presentation skills to help me make a slide deck. First confirm the audience, setting, duration, core message, and available source material; then create a slide-by-slide outline, visual direction, and narrative flow, and generate an editable PPTX once the requirements are sufficient. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My presentation topic:
prompts.searchLiterature:
Use real literature-search skills to find evidence for me. First clarify the research question, PICO/keywords, databases, date range, and eligibility criteria; then provide verifiable papers, search strings, evidence summaries, and research gaps. Never invent titles, DOIs, or citations. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My topic:
prompts.downloadLiterature:
Use literature-acquisition skills to download the requested full text. First identify the target papers from the supplied titles, DOIs, PMIDs, PMCIDs, arXiv IDs, literature list, or Zotero records. Then check existing project files, Zotero attachments, PMC/Europe PMC, Unpaywall, arXiv, and other lawful open sources in that order; never bypass a paywall. Save the files and report the source, status, local path, and failure reason, and parse PDFs when needed. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Literature to download:
prompts.dataAnalysis:
Use data-analysis skills to help me analyze data. Inspect the data structure, variable types, missingness, outliers, and analysis objective first; include database-specific analysis, baseline tables, descriptive statistics, tests, or models as needed, then complete diagnostics, visualization, effect-size reporting, and reproducible outputs. Never invent results without inspecting real data. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My data or analysis question:
prompts.experimentLog:
Use the experiment-log skill to organize this experiment. Read the supplied images, audio, or text; standardize experiment IDs, sample batches, equipment, conditions, observations, results, anomalies, and next actions; and produce a traceable Markdown log with YAML frontmatter. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Experiment materials:
prompts.researchDesign:
Use research-design skills to help me develop a study plan. Clarify the question, PICO, population, exposure/intervention, outcome, time zero, and available data; then define eligibility criteria, variables, bias control, sample size, and the statistical analysis plan. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My research question:
prompts.databaseExtraction:
Use database-extraction skills to help me obtain real data. Confirm the research question, target database, cohort structure, and required variables; locate real tables and fields, verify timeline and coding semantics, and extract only task-relevant data while preserving source paths and reproducibility records. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My database task:
prompts.baselineTableQuick:
Use baseline-table skills to create a submission-ready Table 1. Confirm the grouping variable, continuous and categorical variables, weighting or matching needs, missing-data display, and statistical conventions; then produce the table, SMD/group tests, and manuscript-ready methods text. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My data and groups:
prompts.submitManuscript:
Use the relevant submission skills to help me submit a manuscript. First confirm the target journal, article type, manuscript status, and available files; then check journal requirements, the submission checklist, formatting, references, cover letter, declarations, and final submission risks. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My submission task:
prompts.proposalWriting:
Use research-proposal skills to draft or revise a proposal, opening report, research plan, or grant application. Establish the evidence base, central argument, and aims before organizing the technical route, innovation, feasibility, risk alternatives, and quality review. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My proposal task:
prompts.paperToPatent:
Use the paper-to-patent skill to identify protectable technical points from papers, reports, code, figures, or inventor notes; build a feature-to-evidence map; compare prior art; draft a technical disclosure or Chinese invention patent; and audit claim support and consistency. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My paper or technical materials:
prompts.reviewManuscript:
Use mock-review skills to assess this manuscript from an independent referee perspective before submission. Evaluate novelty, significance, technical soundness, statistics, evidence, and presentation; then produce Major Concerns, Minor Comments, and blocking flags. Do not write an author rebuttal. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Manuscript to review:
prompts.statisticsAudit:
Use statistical-audit skills to inspect the manuscript's reporting. Check sample size, replicate type, randomization, blinding, model assumptions, effect sizes, confidence intervals, p values, multiple comparisons, figure legends, and Results wording, and provide directly actionable revisions. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Content to audit:
prompts.replyReviewers:
Use nature-response to process the editor decision and reviewer comments. First confirm Major Revision or Minor Revision from the decision letter; number, classify, and track editor and reviewer items separately; keep mutually blind reviewers isolated; draft point-by-point responses; and map every claimed change to the manuscript. Never invent experiments, citations, line numbers, or completed changes; mark missing information as AUTHOR_INPUT_NEEDED. Available skills: {{skills}}.

Decision letter, reviewer comments, and current manuscript:
prompts.scientificFigure:
Use scientific-figure skills to create a submission-ready figure. Identify the figure type that best matches the data and conclusion, define layout, palette, statistical annotations, legend, panel labels, and export specifications, and generate a reproducible figure from real data. Available skills: {{skills}}.

The figure I need:
prompts.mechanismDiagram:
Use scientific-schematic skills to create a mechanism diagram. Organize the entities, pathways, causal or regulatory relationships, evidence strength, and visual hierarchy, then produce a manuscript- or grant-ready structure and high-quality image prompt. Available skills: {{skills}}.

The mechanism I need to show:
prompts.graphicalAbstractQuick:
Use graphical-abstract skills to compress the research question, data source, core method, key finding, and significance into one submission-ready visual with a clear layout and concise text. Available skills: {{skills}}.

My research content:
prompts.mindMap:
Use scientific-schematic skills to organize the current topic, paper, or plan as a clear mind map. Identify the central question and hierarchy, then structure branches, dependencies, evidence, and next actions. Available skills: {{skills}}.

What I need to organize:
prompts.todayTasks:
Based on the current project, existing conversation, and explicit deadlines, organize today's tasks. Rank them as must finish, important progress, or deferrable; include estimated time, dependencies, and the next action. Point out missing evidence instead of inventing tasks.

Items to include today:
prompts.replyAdvisor:
Help me reply to my advisor. First identify the questions, feedback, tasks, and deadlines in the advisor's message; then draft a polite, concise, natural response that is ready to send, followed by a separate action-item list. Do not invent progress or commitments. Available skills: {{skills}}.

The advisor's message or content to reply to:
prompts.createKnowledgeBase:
Help me create a searchable, maintainable knowledge base. First confirm its topic, source materials, file formats, update process, and use cases; then organize the documents, design categories and metadata, deduplicate and chunk the content, and create a structure suitable for retrieval and question answering. Available skills: {{skills}}.

The knowledge base I want to create:
prompts.researchInsights:
Use research-monitoring skills to summarize recent developments. Confirm the topic, time window, sources, and exclusion rules; then provide verifiable new papers, trend changes, important debates, potential research topics, and recommendations for continued monitoring. Available skills: {{skills}}.

The field I want to track:
prompts.watchNews:
First use agent-reach to look up news and platform updates. Do not invent posts from memory. Confirm the topic, platforms, and time window; if I do not name a platform, choose Xiaohongshu, Bilibili, or other public pages that fit the task. Prefer agent-reach to search, read, and summarize real content. If agent-reach is unavailable, the platform has no working backend, or it returns no content, fall back to the isolated agent browser: use browser_open to open pages and browser_snapshot / browser_action to search, browse, and filter. When you find posts, videos, or articles worth viewing, keep show_in_sidebar=true or use browser_show so they open in the sidebar browser for me. Finish with a source-by-source list of titles, links, timestamps, key points, and evidence you actually saw. If login, CAPTCHA, or the browser blocks a page, say so and use browser_show to hand the URL to the sidebar. Do not post, comment, like, or log in on my behalf. Available skills: {{skills}}.

What I want to look at:
prompts.createSkill:
Use skill-creator to build a reusable Skill. First define its triggers, scope, inputs and outputs, workflow, required references or scripts, and validation approach; then create or update SKILL.md and the necessary resources according to the standard. Available skills: {{skills}}.

routePrompts.statisticalModeling:
Please help me with "Statistical modeling & testing". First route the task to the smallest necessary skill set based on the task details. Do not call all statistical modeling skills by default.

Routing rules:
1. Statistical analysis plan, test selection, hypotheses, effect sizes, power, APA or manuscript reporting: use statistical-analysis.
2. Directly running specified t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square, correlations, non-parametric tests, or multiple-testing correction: use data-stats-analysis.
3. Linear, logistic, Poisson/negative binomial, mixed models, ARIMA/time series, robust standard errors, diagnostics, and coefficient tables: use statsmodels.
4. Cox, KM, survival outcomes, censored data, competing risks, or time-dependent AUC: use scikit-survival.
5. Bayesian, hierarchical, MCMC, prior/posterior predictive checks, or uncertainty quantification: use pymc.
6. UK Biobank-specific cohort fields, endpoints, covariates, and sensitivity analysis: use ukb-cohort-analysis.
7. Integrating finished statistical outputs, tables, figures, and Results text: use medhelp-experiment-analysis.

Default principles: for unclear clinical/epidemiologic analysis, start with statistical-analysis; add statsmodels, scikit-survival, or pymc only once the modeling target is clear.
